nodes.summary: Every natural number $n > 161$ is the sum of the elements of some finite set of primes $p$ with $p \equiv 5 \pmod 6$; that is, $n$ is a sum of distinct primes of the form $6k - 1$.
nodes.title: Makowski's theorem on sums of distinct primes of the form $6k - 1$

nodes.summary: For every natural number $x \ge 7$ there is a prime $p$ with $x < p < 2x$ and $p \equiv 5 \pmod 6$, that is, a prime of the form $6k - 1$ strictly between $x$ and $2x$.
nodes.title: Breusch's theorem for primes of the form $6k - 1$
